WESTERN.meaning: Relating to or characteristic of the western parts of the world or the West as opposed to the eastern or oriental parts.

WET.meaning: Covered with or containing water or another liquid.

WHALE.meaning: A very large person; impressive in size or qualities.

WHARF.meaning: A platform built out from the shore into the water and supported by piles; provides access to ships and boats.

WHAT.meaning: Used to ask for information about a thing or event.

WHATEVER.meaning: One or some or every or all without specification.

WHEAT.meaning: Annual or biennial grass having erect flower spikes and light brown grains.

WHEEL.meaning: A simple machine consisting of a circular frame with spokes (or a solid disc) that can rotate on a shaft or axle (as in vehicles or other machines).

WHEELED.meaning: Having wheels; often used in combination.

WHEELER.meaning: Someone who makes and repairs wooden wheels.

WHEELS.meaning: Plural of wheel: A simple machine consisting of a circular frame with spokes (or a solid disc) that can rotate on a shaft or axle (as in vehicles or other machines).

WHEN.meaning: At what time, or at the time that something happens.

WHICH.meaning: Used to ask or specify one or more from a known set.

WHIFF.meaning: A short light gust of air.

WHILE.meaning: A period of indeterminate length (usually short) marked by some action or condition.

WHIP.meaning: Beat severely with a whip or rod.

WHIPPING.meaning: Beating with a whip or strap or rope as a form of punishment.

WHISKEY.meaning: A liquor made from fermented mash of grain.

WHISKY.meaning: A liquor made from fermented mash of grain.

WHISPER.meaning: Speak softly; in a low voice.

WHITE.meaning: Being of the achromatic color of maximum lightness; having little or no hue owing to reflection of almost all incident light.

WHITES.meaning: Plural of white: The quality or state of the achromatic color of greatest lightness (bearing the least resemblance to black).

WHO.meaning: Used to ask which person, or to refer to a person just mentioned.

WHOLE.meaning: Including all components without exception; being one unit or constituting the full amount or extent or duration; complete.

WHOLLY.meaning: To a complete degree or to the full or entire extent ('whole' is often used informally for 'wholly').

WHOM.meaning: The object form of who: which person receives an action.

WHOOP.meaning: Shout, as if with joy or enthusiasm.

WICKED.meaning: Morally bad in principle or practice.

WICKET.meaning: Cricket equipment consisting of a set of three stumps topped by crosspieces; used in playing cricket.

WIDE.meaning: Having great (or a certain) extent from one side to the other.

WIDEN.meaning: Become broader or wider or more extensive.

WIDOW.meaning: A woman whose husband is dead especially one who has not remarried.

WIDTH.meaning: The extent of something from side to side.

WIFE.meaning: A married woman; a man's partner in marriage.

WILD.meaning: Marked by extreme lack of restraint or control.

WILDFIRE.meaning: A raging and rapidly spreading conflagration.

WILDLIFE.meaning: All living things (except people) that are undomesticated.

WILDLY.meaning: To an extreme or greatly exaggerated degree.

WILL.meaning: The capability of conscious choice and decision and intention.

WILLOW.meaning: Any of numerous deciduous trees and shrubs of the genus Salix.

WIN.meaning: Be the winner in a contest or competition; be victorious.

WIND.meaning: Air moving (sometimes with considerable force) from an area of high pressure to an area of low pressure.

WINDING.meaning: Marked by repeated turns and bends.

WINDOW.meaning: A framework of wood or metal that contains a glass windowpane and is built into a wall or roof to admit light or air.

WINDS.meaning: Plural of wind: Air moving (sometimes with considerable force) from an area of high pressure to an area of low pressure.

WINDY.meaning: Abounding in or exposed to the wind or breezes.

WINES.meaning: Plural of wine: Fermented juice (of grapes especially).

WING.meaning: A movable organ for flying (one of a pair).

WINGED.meaning: Having wings or as if having wings of a specified kind.

WINGS.meaning: A means of flight or ascent.

WINNER.meaning: The contestant who wins the contest.

WINNERS.meaning: Plural of winner: The contestant who wins the contest.

WINS.meaning: Plural of win: A victory (as in a race or other competition).

WINTER.meaning: The coldest season of the year; in the northern hemisphere it extends from the winter solstice to the vernal equinox.

WIPED.meaning: A grammatical form of wipe: Rub with a circular motion.

WIRE.meaning: Ligament made of metal and used to fasten things or make cages or fences etc.

WIRED.meaning: Equipped with wire or wires especially for electric or telephone service.

WIRES.meaning: Plural of wire: Ligament made of metal and used to fasten things or make cages or fences etc.

WIRING.meaning: A circuit of wires for the distribution of electricity.

WISDOM.meaning: Accumulated knowledge or erudition or enlightenment.

WISE.meaning: Having or prompted by wisdom or discernment.

WISHED.meaning: A grammatical form of wish: Hope for; have a wish.

WISHES.meaning: Plural of wish: A specific feeling of desire.

WITH.meaning: Accompanied by, together with, or using something.

WITHDRAW.meaning: Pull back or move away or backward.

WITHHOLD.meaning: Hold back; refuse to hand over or share.

WITTY.meaning: Combining clever conception and facetious expression.

WIVES.meaning: Plural of wife: A married woman; a man's partner in marriage.

WIZARD.meaning: Someone who is dazzlingly skilled in any field.

WOLF.meaning: Any of various predatory carnivorous canine mammals of North America and Eurasia that usually hunt in packs.

WOLVES.meaning: Plural of wolf: Any of various predatory carnivorous canine mammals of North America and Eurasia that usually hunt in packs.

WOMAN.meaning: An adult female person (as opposed to a man).

WOMB.meaning: A hollow muscular organ in the pelvic cavity of females; contains the developing fetus.

WON.meaning: The past tense of win: achieved victory in a contest.

WONDER.meaning: Have a wish or desire to know something.

WONDERED.meaning: A grammatical form of wonder: Have a wish or desire to know something.

WONDERS.meaning: Plural of wonder: The feeling aroused by something strange and surprising.

WOOD.meaning: The hard fibrous lignified substance under the bark of trees.

WOODED.meaning: Covered with growing trees and bushes etc.

WOODEN.meaning: Made or consisting of (entirely or in part) or employing wood.

WOODLAND.meaning: Land that is covered with trees and shrubs.

WOODS.meaning: The trees and other plants in a large densely wooded area.

WOODWORK.meaning: Work made of wood; especially moldings or stairways or furniture.

WOODY.meaning: Made of or containing or resembling wood.

WOOL.meaning: A fabric made from the hair of sheep.

WORD.meaning: A unit of language with a meaning, spoken or written.

WORDING.meaning: The manner in which something is expressed in words.

WORK.meaning: Activity directed toward making or doing something.

WORKED.meaning: A grammatical form of work: Exert oneself by doing mental or physical work for a purpose or out of necessity.

WORKER.meaning: A person who works at a specific occupation.

WORKERS.meaning: Plural of worker: A person who works at a specific occupation.

WORKINGS.meaning: The internal mechanism of a device.

WORKLOAD.meaning: Work that a person is expected to do in a specified time.

WORKOUT.meaning: The activity of exerting your muscles in various ways to keep fit.

WORKS.meaning: Buildings for carrying on industrial labor.

WORKSHOP.meaning: Small workplace where handcrafts or manufacturing are done.

WORLDLY.meaning: Characteristic of or devoted to the temporal world as opposed to the spiritual world.

WORLDS.meaning: Plural of world: Everything that exists anywhere.

WORM.meaning: Any of numerous relatively small elongated soft-bodied animals especially of the phyla Annelida and Chaetognatha and Nematoda and Nemertea and Platyhelminthes; also many insect larvae.

WORN.meaning: Affected by wear; damaged by long use.

WORRIED.meaning: Afflicted with or marked by anxious uneasiness or trouble or grief.

WORRIES.meaning: Plural of worry: Something or someone that causes anxiety; a source of unhappiness.

WORRY.meaning: Be worried, concerned, anxious, troubled, or uneasy.

WORSE.meaning: (comparative of 'bad') inferior to another in quality or condition or desirability.

WORST.meaning: (superlative of 'bad') most wanting in quality or value or condition.

WORTH.meaning: Worthy of being treated in a particular way; (often used ironically).

WORTHY.meaning: Having worth or merit or value; being honorable or admirable.

WOUND.meaning: An injury to living tissue (especially an injury involving a cut or break in the skin).

WOUNDED.meaning: Suffering from physical injury especially that suffered in battle.

WOUNDS.meaning: Plural of wound: An injury to living tissue (especially an injury involving a cut or break in the skin).

WOVEN.meaning: Made or constructed by interlacing threads or strips of material or other elements into a whole.

WRAP.meaning: Arrange or fold as a cover or protection.

WRAPPED.meaning: Covered with or as if with clothes or a wrap or cloak.

WRAPPING.meaning: The covering (usually paper or cellophane) in which something is wrapped.

WRATH.meaning: Intense anger (usually on an epic scale).

WREATH.meaning: Flower arrangement consisting of a circular band of foliage or flowers for ornamental purposes.

WRECKAGE.meaning: The remaining parts of something that has been wrecked.

WRECKING.meaning: The event of a structure being completely demolished and leveled.

WRENCH.meaning: Twist or pull violently or suddenly, especially so as to remove (something) from that to which it is attached or from where it originates.

WRESTLE.meaning: Combat to overcome an opposing tendency or force.

WRESTLER.meaning: Combatant who tries to throw opponent to the ground.

WRETCHED.meaning: Of very poor quality or condition.

WRIGHT.meaning: Someone who makes or repairs something (usually used in combination).

WRIST.meaning: A joint between the distal end of the radius and the proximal row of carpal bones.

WRITER.meaning: Writes (books or stories or articles or the like) professionally (for pay).

WRITERS.meaning: Plural of writer: Writes (books or stories or articles or the like) professionally (for pay).

WRITES.meaning: A grammatical form of write: Produce a literary work.

WRITING.meaning: The act of creating written works.

WRITTEN.meaning: Set down in writing in any of various ways.

WRONG.meaning: Not correct; not in conformity with fact or truth.

WROUGHT.meaning: Shaped to fit by or as if by altering the contours of a pliable mass (as by work or effort).

YACHT.meaning: An expensive vessel propelled by sail or power and used for cruising or racing.

YAHOO.meaning: A person who is not very intelligent or interested in culture.

YANG.meaning: The bright positive masculine principle in Chinese dualistic cosmology.

YARD.meaning: A unit of length equal to 3 feet; defined as 91.44 centimeters; originally taken to be the average length of a stride.

YARDS.meaning: Plural of yard: A unit of length equal to 3 feet; defined as 91.44 centimeters; originally taken to be the average length of a stride.

YARN.meaning: The act of giving an account describing incidents or a course of events.

YEAR.meaning: A period of time containing 365 (or 366) days.

YEARBOOK.meaning: A book published annually by the graduating class of a high school or college usually containing photographs of faculty and graduating students.

YEARLY.meaning: A reference book that is published regularly once every year.

YEAST.meaning: A commercial leavening agent containing yeast cells; used to raise the dough in making bread and for fermenting beer or whiskey.

YELLING.meaning: Uttering a loud inarticulate cry as of pain or excitement.

YELLOW.meaning: Of the color intermediate between green and orange in the color spectrum; of something resembling the color of an egg yolk.

YIELD.meaning: Be the cause or source of.

YIELDING.meaning: Inclined to yield to argument or influence or control.

YIELDS.meaning: Plural of yield: Production of a certain amount.

YOGA.meaning: Hindu discipline aimed at training the consciousness for a state of perfect spiritual insight and tranquility that is achieved through the three paths of actions and knowledge and devotion.

YOGURT.meaning: A custard-like food made from curdled milk.

YOU.meaning: The person or people being spoken or written to.

YOUNG.meaning: (used of living things especially persons) in an early period of life or development or growth.

YOUNGER.meaning: Used of the younger of two persons of the same name especially used to distinguish a son from his father.

YOUTH.meaning: A young person (especially a young man or boy).

YOUTHFUL.meaning: Suggestive of youth; vigorous and fresh.

YUAN.meaning: The basic unit of money in China.

YUMMY.meaning: Extremely pleasing to the sense of taste.

ZEBRA.meaning: Any of several fleet black-and-white striped African equines.

ZIP.meaning: To fasten with a zipper, or to move very quickly.

ZIPPER.meaning: A fastener for locking together two toothed edges by means of a sliding tab.

ZODIAC.meaning: A belt-shaped region in the heavens on either side to the ecliptic; divided into 12 constellations or signs for astrological purposes.

ZOMBIE.meaning: A dead body that has been brought back to life by a supernatural force.

ZONE.meaning: A locally circumscribed place characterized by some distinctive features.

ZONES.meaning: Plural of zone: A locally circumscribed place characterized by some distinctive features.

ZONING.meaning: Dividing an area into zones or sections reserved for different purposes such as residence and business and manufacturing etc.

ZOO.meaning: The facility where wild animals are housed for exhibition.
